long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Hay River on Great Slave Lake, Barry Stewart grew up around boats, hockey and the small building-supply company founded by his father, Don. He returned to the family enterprise after playing junior hockey and became president at 23. Moving south to Edmonton, he created a base from which Igloo could serve northern communities and the Alberta construction market.

Stewart transformed that inherited platform through acquisitions and vertical expansion. Igloo added truss manufacturing, drywall distribution and installation, then widened its product range into flooring, siding, electrical and lighting. The company now operates across Edmonton, Yellowknife and Cornwall, shipping complete building packages over highways, ice roads and barges. As chairman, Stewart remains the family steward while a professional president directs daily operations.
